content:
Plan for Phase 11 sonicgrid-triage-sync (B3): docs/phases/sonicgrid-triage-sync.md.

Builds against sonicgrid S2's contract documentation/BUGALIZER-TRIAGE-ENDPOINTS.md (sonicgrid main 9ce7fe50, PR #618; S2 hosted acceptance 2026-09-30). Direction: Aegis rulings E1-E6 (2026-09-30).

Shape: one off-by-default sync task (15 s tick) per project with ingest_config.triage_credential_env set. Each tick it (a) walks GET /actions from no cursor to null, claims and executes actions in process against Bugalizer internals, and applies the contract's recovery table from a durable triage_actions ledger; (b) pushes PUT /results/{bugId} for sonicgrid-sourced reports whose payload fingerprint changed.

Decisions to review (Summary section): D-A the allowlist gates analyze_cloud always and the fix step of fix_and_open_pr only when Stage 4 resolves to a paid provider. D-B the revision is issued by B3 from a payload fingerprint (max(last+1, epoch µs)), because bug_reports.updated_at isn't bumped by analysis/PR rows. D-C attribution is key_source=env, key_ref=sonicgrid:<userId> via an internal-only propose_fix parameter (alternative: a requested_by column). D-D the requester email isn't stored. D-E propose_fix / process_localization / run_local_analysis return an outcome value so B3 can tell failed from deferred from not-claimed.

Also in this change: docs/roadmap.md bookkeeping. Phase 8 status now starts with "Complete:", and the (B2)/(B3, proposed)/(B4…)/(proposed) notes moved out of the Phase 8/9/11/12 headings so the slugs are clean (tagteam roadmap ready now lists sonicgrid-triage-sync). Phase 11 status points at the plan.

Verification: plan cycle, docs only; no code or tests changed. Code facts behind the plan were checked by reading db.py (analyses schema, _now, updated_at writers), api/reports.py analyze_report, fix_proposer.propose_fix, orchestrator, and pull_request.OpenPrError.

Reviewed the plan against sonicgrid documentation/BUGALIZER-TRIAGE-ENDPOINTS.md, the E1-E6 direction on QA branch docs/bugalizer-sonicgrid-triage-direction, and the existing Bugalizer execution paths. REQUEST_CHANGES:

1. [P1] Enforce genuinely local execution for analyze_local (plan section 4, lines 214 and 230-232). resolve_local_llm in src/bugalizer/llm/client.py accepts project.llm_provider, including anthropic; the project model does not restrict it to ollama. Calling run_local_analysis without an allowlist check can therefore spend BOWIE's cloud key for a non-allowlisted user, and recovery would classify that paid work as safe to repeat. Specify that B3 analyze_local refuses non-local resolved providers before dispatch, or pins an explicitly local configuration throughout its run. Also pin/revalidate the authorized Stage 4 configuration at execution so a project change between authorization and provider resolution cannot turn an approved local fix into a paid one. Add non-allowlisted + project.llm_provider=anthropic and configuration-change tests.

2. [P1] Serialize all sync entry points and reserve dispatch ownership atomically (sections 1, 3, 6). Both the background tick and POST triage-sync/run can walk the same pending action. Sonicgrid explicitly returns 200 changed:false to the second claimant; section 3 currently tells both to dispatch. Specify a shared per-project tick lock and an atomic action/task/slot reservation, with existing ledger state taking precedence even when the fetched action was pending. Define the single-consumer deployment constraint and how two configured projects pointing at the same source are handled. Test overlapping manual/background ticks and repeated changed:false acknowledgements: one dispatch, one ledger outcome, concurrency bound retained.

3. [P1] Make compound recovery and timeout behaviour explicit (section 3, lines 174-188; section 4). Persist fix:done and its exact proposal id before attempting open-pr, and on restart resume only the PR step. Otherwise a crash after the fix can re-enter propose_fix, receive already_proposed, and incorrectly refuse the fix this action actually completed. Define how recovered evidence is associated with this action rather than another worker/manual run, and what happens to a still-running task after its action times out: a late fix completion must not start the PR step or overwrite the terminal ledger outcome. Add crash tests after fix persistence/before PR, after branch push, and timeout followed by late completion. Keep the report/task reservation until side effects have actually stopped.

4. [P2] Retry terminal acknowledgements from the local ledger independently of GET /actions (section 3, lines 166-185). If Sonicgrid commits done but its response is lost, that action disappears from the open-only listing. Recovery driven only by listed actions will never retry it or set terminal_acked. Add a per-tick drain of finished, unacked ledger entries; test a committed terminal POST with a dropped response followed by an empty action listing and a process restart.

5. [P2] Include bugalizerUpdatedAt in change detection (section 2). The fingerprint currently hashes public + admin only. A later completed analysis with identical output changes the required analysed-at timestamp but triggers no push, contradicting the stated new-analysis-row success criterion and push-after-change rule. Fingerprint the complete meaningful payload excluding revision, and keep one persisted revision/payload association for retries. Test an identical-result new analysis with a newer timestamp.

D-B (durable monotonic revisions), D-C (env plus sonicgrid user key_ref), D-D (email in memory only), and D-E (explicit outcomes) are reasonable. D-A matches the endpoint contract for analyze_cloud and fix_and_open_pr, subject to the execution safeguards above. No tests run: this is a plan review; source and contract inspection only.

r2: all five r1 findings addressed in docs/phases/sonicgrid-triage-sync.md (a "Revision r2" paragraph in the Summary maps each one).

1 [P1] Local execution: D-A now defines "paid" as any stage the action would use resolving to a provider other than ollama, so analyze_local on a project with llm_provider=anthropic needs the allowlist and counts as a cloud kind for recovery. New §4a pins provider/model at authorization (stored in triage_actions.pinned_llm). Local stages take it through run_local_analysis → process_triaged/process_localization → triage_report/localize_report, which already accept explicit provider/model. Stage 4 takes it as a provider/model-only LLMOverride (no key, so key_source stays env). Re-dispatch uses the stored pin. Tests added in success criterion 5.

2 [P1] Ownership: §1 adds a per-project tick lock shared by the loop and POST …/run (409 tick_in_progress), and one consumer per sonicgrid source (PATCH 409 triage_source_in_use; existing duplicates are skipped with duplicate_triage_source; multi-instance unsupported). §3 adds an atomic reservation: INSERT phase='reserved' in the same transaction that takes the slot, before POST claimed. Only the reservation holder dispatches, so a repeated changed:false never dispatches twice. The ledger phase takes precedence over the listed state. Tests in success criterion 7.

3 [P1] Compound/timeout: §3a. fix_and_open_pr writes phase='fix_done' plus fix_proposal_id plus the fix step in one write before open-pr; recovery resumes only the PR step and never re-calls propose_fix. Evidence comes from a new nullable trigger_ref column on analyses and fix_proposals, set only by B3 runs, so manual or worker runs are never adopted. The terminal outcome is written once by a conditional update; a late task records late_outcome only and re-checks its row before open-pr. Slot and report are held until the task actually exits. Tests in success criterion 6.

4 [P2] Terminal drain: §3. Every tick POSTs every finished row with terminal_acked=0, independent of GET /actions. 409 with the same currentState counts as acked; any other 409 or a 404 is acked with an error surfaced. Test in success criterion 7a.

5 [P2] Fingerprint: §2. It covers the whole payload except revision, including bugalizerUpdatedAt. Fingerprint, revision and payload are stored together before the PUT, and an unacked push is resent with the same revision and payload. Test in success criterion 1.

Verification: plan only, no code. The pinning claim was checked against triage_report/localize_report (explicit provider/model args) and resolve_local_llm (accepts any project.llm_provider).

r2 resolves the prior serialization, compound checkpoint/late-completion, terminal-drain, and timestamp-fingerprint findings. Provider/model pinning also closes the authorization/configuration race. Two narrow inconsistencies remain:

1. [P2] Separate recovery classification from actual paid-provider classification (section 3, lines 225-234). D-A defines paid solely by provider != ollama, but the recovery algorithm uses only paid to decide whether uncertain dispatch may be repeated. Thus analyze_cloud on BOWIE's Ollama provider will be automatically re-dispatched after an intent-only crash. The endpoint contract explicitly names analyze_cloud in the fail-without-retry branch, regardless of provider, and success criterion 6 still promises that behaviour. Define the recovery predicate as kind == analyze_cloud OR pinned paid work (with fix_done resuming only the safe PR step). Test analyze_cloud intent-only recovery on both Ollama and a paid provider; neither starts another LLM call.

2. [P2] Extend requester attribution to the newly supported paid analyze_local path (D-C, section 4 lines 320-322, section 4a). r2 now allows an allowlisted analyze_local request to use anthropic, but attribution_ref is still specified only on propose_fix. Triage and localization write token usage directly (pipeline/triage.py and pipeline/localizer.py), so these cloud charges would have no sonicgrid user key_ref, violating D-C and success criterion 8. Thread attribution_ref through run_local_analysis and both local stages to every token_usage_create call, including both localization passes; existing worker/API callers retain current defaults. Add an allowlisted paid analyze_local test asserting env + sonicgrid:<userId> on all usage rows. Alternatively, keep B3 analyze_local strictly Ollama and explicitly refuse non-local providers, which avoids introducing this paid path.

No tests run: plan review only. No additional direction ruling is needed; these reconcile the revised algorithm with its existing contract and stated success criteria.

r3: both r2 findings addressed in docs/phases/sonicgrid-triage-sync.md (a "Revision r3" note in the Summary).

1 [P2] Recovery predicate: the ledger's paid column is replaced by no_auto_retry = kind == analyze_cloud OR a paid fix step (D-A, §3 ledger schema and the intent-only rule). analyze_cloud is never auto-re-dispatched on any provider; a fix_and_open_pr at fix_done still resumes only the PR step. Success criterion 6 now tests analyze_cloud intent-only recovery with both an ollama and a paid pinned fix provider, with no second LLM call in either case.

2 [P2] Paid analyze_local: took your alternative. A B3 analyze_local is refused for every requester, allowlisted or not, when the pinned triage or localize provider isn't ollama (D-A, §4 table, §4a). There's no paid local path, so attribution_ref stays on propose_fix only. Success criterion 5 tests the refusal for an allowlisted and a non-allowlisted user with project.llm_provider=anthropic and no LLM call.

Verification: plan only, no code.

Approved. Reviewed the r3 plan and submission against the remaining r2 findings and the previously reviewed endpoint contract and E1-E6 direction.

Both r2 findings are resolved: no_auto_retry explicitly includes analyze_cloud regardless of provider, while fix_done resumes only the PR step; B3 analyze_local refuses non-Ollama providers for every requester, eliminating the paid local path and its attribution gap. Success criteria 5 and 6 explicitly cover these cases. The prior safeguards remain: pinned provider/model, serialized ticks and action reservations, action-tagged recovery evidence, compound checkpoints and immutable terminal outcomes, independent terminal acknowledgement drain, and full-payload fingerprints with persisted revision/payload pairs.

D-A through D-E are accepted as specified. Implementation should now follow this plan and its automated success criteria. No tests run: documentation-only plan review. BOWIE acceptance remains a separate post-implementation step, with the B2 repository token dependency documented.
